events.title: GitLab admins urged to patch critical RCE flaw (CVE-2026-97229)
events.summary: GitLab has disclosed a critical integer-overflow remote code execution vulnerability in its CI/CD regular expression compiler, affecting self-managed Community and Enterprise Edition instances. The flaw, CVE-2026-97229, has a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and is listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
events.why_it_matters: With a CVSS score of 10.0 and inclusion on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list, this flaw is being actively exploited, so self-managed GitLab instances are at immediate risk. Successful exploitation gives remote attackers arbitrary code execution on GitLab servers, potentially exposing source code and build pipelines. Administrators of GitLab CE and EE should apply available patches without delay.

reasons: The event is reported by Australian outlet CyberDaily AU.
No Australian organisations, people, government, or infrastructure are named in the record.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2026-97229 as exploited in the wild, added 2026-10-29, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2026-11-01.
CVE-2026-97229 is rated 10.0 (critical) under CVSS 3.1 by the CNA that assigned it.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-97229 being exploited in the next 30 days at 27%.
8 independent sources report this event.

events.title: Let’s Encrypt TLS certificate lifetimes to drop from 90 to 64 days starting February 2027
events.summary: Websites that rely on Let’s Encrypt will soon have to renew their TLS certificates more often. Starting February 10, 2027, the certificate authority will issue certificates valid for 64 days by default, down from 90 days. Subscribers who already use Let’s Encrypt’s optional 45-day or 6-day certificates are not affected. events.title: [INFO] Chromium: CVE-2025-12441 Out of bounds read in V8
events.summary: A new out-of-bounds read vulnerability (CVE-2025-12441) was identified in Chromium’s V8 engine.
events.why_it_matters: The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 4.3, indicating moderate risk; defenders should monitor for exploitation and consider patching Chromium components. The low EPSs value (0.00206) suggests limited exploitation likelihood, but the medium CVSS warrants vigilance.

claims.text: CVE-2025-12441 is rated 4.3 (medium) under CVSS 3.1 by CISA in the CVE record.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2025-12441 being exploited in the next 30 days at under 1%.
